stories.title: Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder
stories.summary: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity to murder journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Almost nine years after the attack, the question of who ordered her death remains unanswered.

stories.title: Meloni marks government longevity at Bari rally with 2027 vote in sight
stories.summary: The durability of Meloni’s coalition has been a rarity in postwar Italy, where governments have often fallen before the end of their mandates. Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni is celebrating in Bari four years in government, marking the longest-serving government in the history of the Italian Republic. On 4 September, her government reached 1,413 days in office, becoming the longest-serving single administration in the history of the Italian Republic and surpassing the 1,412-day record set by Silvio Berlusconi's second government. Speaking to supporters, Meloni presented the longevity record as evidence of the stability and cohesion of her right-wing coalition. “It is no coincidence that the three longest-serving governments in the history of the Italian Republic are all center-right governments,” she said. “Stability is our first great reform,” Meloni added, arguing that political continuity had enabled her government to pursue economic and foreign policy goals that might have proved difficult under Italy’s traditionally short-lived administrations. In Bari, Meloni touted several achievements, from the government's longevity to the results of its reforms, in a speech that laid the groundwork for the campaign ahead of the 2027 elections. "The most stable government is not necessarily the most capable one. The most stable government is simply the one that has had more time than others to be judged." According to the latest YouTrend poll, published on 4 September, Brothers of Italy stands at 26.5% in voting intentions. In the 2022 elections, the party won 26.04% of the vote. Among the issues addressed by the premier were justice and security.
